item.title: A flash disk, five paragraphs and a second objection: the treason bail hearing stalls again, and the court rules on Friday whether the raid video stays on the record
item.description: A day after losing its first preliminary objection, the State raised another at the Lusaka High Court on Wednesday 11 November, asking the three-judge panel to strike five paragraphs and a video recording from the affidavit filed by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused. The defence says the footage shows the raid on Zulu's home and answers the State's flight-risk claim. The court adjourned to 11:00 on Friday 13 November to rule, then hear the bail plea. In the sedition case, The Zambian Observer reported that the two dismissed their lawyers.

item.title: Ordered to court at nine, not produced: the State says Jay Jay Banda's doctor will not let him leave Maina Soko, and the judge demands a medical report before Friday
item.description: Judge Geoffrey Mulenga had ordered the State to bring the former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel Jay Jay Banda before the Lusaka High Court at 09:00 on Wednesday 11 November to explain the circumstances of his detention. He was not brought. The Attorney General's office said the doctor treating him at Maina Soko Military Medical Centre had not authorised his movement, and the judge ordered a medical report. The court is expected to rule on Friday on whether the habeas corpus hearing moves to the hospital.

item.title: US$30.89 billion owed, US$275 million saved: external debt fell 5% after the Eurobond buyback, Musokotwane tells Parliament, as the IMF board weighs a US$1.46 billion programme
item.description: Central government debt stood at US$30.89 billion at the end of June 2026, split almost evenly between domestic and external borrowing, the Finance Minister told the National Assembly on Tuesday 10 November. External debt fell from US$16.15 billion in December to US$15.35 billion, mainly because the Treasury bought back about US$1.36 billion of its 2053 Eurobond in May at a discount. A staff-level agreement on a new 36-month IMF programme worth US$1.46 billion was reached on 9 October; the Fund's board is expected to decide in December.

item.title: K12,253.72 to keep a Lusaka family of five: the JCTR basket jumps K854 in a month, and the centre says the budget should have taxed copper windfalls, not wage earners
item.description: The Jesuit Centre for Theological Reflection's Basic Needs and Nutrition Basket for Lusaka rose 7.5% in October, from K11,399.64 to K12,253.72, driven by vegetables and bananas in the hot season. Its director, Fr Daniel Mutale, says formal workers already carry the heaviest tax load and that the budget's VAT and mobile-money increases will reach the poor; PwC, meanwhile, says households will feel the budget at the till and wants a timetable for K60 billion in unpaid VAT refunds.

item.title: 'A true leader should never take people for granted': from his Choma farm, Hichilema tells MPs who wanted ministries to be grateful for their seats and the party to stay united
item.description: Speaking to supporters who gathered at his farm in Choma on Tuesday 10 November, at the start of a ten-day working holiday in Southern Province, the President told elected leaders and appointees to remain loyal and respectful to the UPND structures that built the party, and told MPs unhappy at being passed over for Cabinet to appreciate that voters elected them, citing the Choma MP Cornelius Mweetwa's decade in the seat. A public thank-you rally in Choma follows on Friday.

item.title: 'Verification and recruitment can run together': Tonse says freezing teacher hiring in 2027 contradicts what the UPND once demanded of the PF; the Treasury says count first
item.description: Muhabi Lungu, acting secretary general of the Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance, told Capital FM that the decision not to recruit teachers next year is a missed chance to bring the pupil-teacher ratio towards 1:25, that the UPND criticised the PF for exactly this, and that education's 13% of the 2027 budget falls short of the 20% benchmark. The Finance Minister said on ZNBC on Sunday that there is no plan to recruit in 2027 until deployment irregularities are resolved and the real staffing gaps are known.

item.title: Planning for a dry season: ZESCO maps 11,630MW by 2030 with hydro down to a third, Kapala tells the REA to connect paid-up customers, and Nkana Water warns Kitwe of rationing
item.description: With an El Niño dry spell forecast for the 2026/27 rains, three strands of the power-and-water story came together this week. ZESCO presented targets to more than double installed capacity from 5,220MW to 11,630MW by 2030, with solar rising to 4,126MW; the Electricity Minister, on his first visit to the Rural Electrification Authority, said paid-up customers must be connected without delay; and Nkana Water cut output at Bulangililo by 18% because the Kafue River is falling.

item.title: One goal to find on Sunday: Nouhoun Koné's 21st-minute strike gives Burkina Faso a 1–0 first-leg lead over Zambia's under-23s in Ouagadougou after a delayed flight
item.description: Chisi Mbewe's side had more of the ball but could not find an equaliser after Koné put the young Étalons ahead in the first half of Wednesday's second-round first leg of the 2027 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. The return is at National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka on Sunday 15 November, the first international in Lusaka since CAF approved the venue; the winner over two legs goes into the final round, on the road to Egypt 2027 and the Los Angeles Olympics.

item.title: Friday the 13th in Ndola: Zambia, second in Group I on three points, meet bottom-placed Burundi without Daka, Banda and Lungu, with the return in Bujumbura four days later
item.description: The first of two AFCON qualifiers against Burundi kicks off at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on Friday 13 November. Zambia have three points from a 3–1 defeat in Algeria and a 2–0 win over Togo; Burundi have one, from a 2–2 draw with Algeria after losing 1–0 in Lomé. Captain Fashion Sakala and the goalkeeping coach Kennedy Mweene arrived on Monday, Kings Kangwa is available only for Tuesday's return leg, and the team doctor says the three injured forwards' recovery runs past the seven-day limit.

item.title: 'Happy heavenly 70th birthday, Dad': Tasila Lungu marks the day her father would have turned seventy, seventeen months after his death and with his remains still in South Africa
item.description: Edgar Chagwa Lungu, Zambia's sixth president, would have been 70 on Wednesday 11 November. His daughter, the former Chawama MP Tasila Lungu, wrote that his love and lessons were still with the family every day. The Zambian Observer noted that more than a year after his death in South Africa on 5 June 2025 his remains have not been buried; South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal ruled in June that the family, not the Zambian government, decides where and how that happens.

item.title: 'Properly before the court': the High Court rejects the State's objection and clears the way for the 18 treason accused to argue for bail, as the sedition bail plea slips to Monday
item.description: A three-judge panel of the Lusaka High Court ruled on Tuesday 10 November that the constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused was properly before it, rejecting the State's argument that it had been started in the wrong registry. Nobody has been released: the ruling only means the application will now be heard. A day earlier, the pair's other bail plea, in the sedition case, was adjourned again after the State said it had a preliminary issue to raise.

item.title: 1,247 in Kitwe and 311 in Ndola: the Copperbelt minister orders 1,558 'excess' teachers out to rural schools, as Musokotwane says there will be no teacher recruitment in 2027
item.description: Emmanuel Kasambo says urban schools on the Copperbelt are carrying 1,558 more teachers than their establishments allow while rural classrooms go without, and has given provincial officials a week to complete the staffing count that will move them. On ZNBC's Sunday Interview the Finance Minister said the government would recruit no teachers next year until it knows where the real gaps are.

item.title: Back after 15 years: Canada reopens its High Commission in Lusaka with US$10.5 million in new support and a cooperation agreement that names critical minerals first
item.description: Canada's Secretary of State for International Development, Randeep Sarai, opened the mission on Monday 9 November alongside Mulambo Haimbe and Situmbeko Musokotwane, announcing US$10.5 million for growth, women's empowerment, energy access and institutions. Zambia had been handled from Dar es Salaam for more than a decade; Corry Van Gaal is the new High Commissioner.

item.title: 'Business should not be done through the courts': Hichilema and Trafigura's chairman agree a reset, with legal disputes to settle and concentrate exports in the President's sights
item.description: President Hichilema received a delegation led by Trafigura's chairman Jeremy Weir at State House on Monday 9 November and said afterwards that the two sides had agreed to reset their relationship. News Diggers reports that he asked for outstanding legal disputes to be resolved and for Zambia to stop exporting mineral concentrates. His former policy adviser Chipokota Mwanawasa was recently appointed the trader's Country Executive Director for Zambia.

item.title: 16,000 megawatts on paper, 4,722 on the grid: Kapala visits the ERB and calls in the developers whose signed power deals cannot find the money to build
item.description: The new Minister of Electricity, Peter Kapala, used a familiarisation visit to the Energy Regulation Board on Monday 9 November to ask why projects with signed power purchase agreements are not reaching financial close. The ERB's chairman put the signed pipeline at more than 16,000 MW; the national target is 10,000 MW of capacity by 2031, from 4,722 MW in October.

item.title: A plea agreement, not yet filed: the State says it has a deal with David Kazadi and two co-accused in the obscene-material case, and the magistrate gives it until close of business
item.description: The trial of the film producer David Kazadi, the social-media figure Mwaka Halwindi and Ruby Muzandu on eight counts of producing, possessing and circulating obscene material was due to start on Tuesday 10 November. Instead the prosecution told the Lusaka Magistrates' Court it had reached an agreement under the Plea Negotiations and Agreements Act. Its terms have not been disclosed; the case returns on 18 November.

item.title: Daka, Lameck Banda and Gamphani Lungu are out of both Burundi games: three injuries, three replacements, and three Europe-based arrivals land in Ndola on the same afternoon
item.description: Patson Daka's ankle, hurt in Hamburg's win over Mönchengladbach on 6 November, has cost Zambia its first-choice striker for Friday's qualifier at Levy Mwanawasa and the return in Bujumbura. Team doctor George Magwende says all three recoveries exceed seven days. Edward Chilufya, Derrick Bulaya and Prince Mumba come in; Chanka Zimba, Joseph Liteta and David Hamansenya flew in on Tuesday.

item.title: A K93 million KCM deal, 40% of the referees' arrears paid and Asanović's debt stretched to 2028: the Times of Zambia sets out FAZ's own account of 18 months of balance-sheet repair
item.description: Eighteen months after Keith Mweemba's executive took office, a Times of Zambia feature lays out what the association says it has done about money: a five-year sponsorship with Konkola Copper Mines, a committee tasked with raising US$30 million in two years, a referees' debt being cleared in instalments and separations from two former coaches without severance. The figures are FAZ's.

item.title: 'Easier to ship from Zambia to London than to Ghana': AfroQuality opens its first Lusaka store at Arcades to sell African brands across African borders
item.description: The pan-African retailer, which already has shops in Accra, Kigali, Nairobi and Dakar, has opened at Arcades Shopping Mall with a pitch to Zambian designers: a shelf in other African capitals. The Zambia Association of Fashion Designers' president Faith Kabende and FNB Zambia's Luyando Mumba spoke at the launch, the Times of Zambia reports.

item.title: Kalambo, Chishimba and the Mwela rock art: the Culture minister visits Kasama and says the Northern Circuit needs roads, marketing and money to help reach five million visitors
item.description: Christopher Chibuye paid a courtesy call on Northern Province Minister Wedden Chileshe on Tuesday 10 November to see the state of the province's heritage sites. He called for investment in heritage infrastructure and better access roads, and said the Northern Circuit could contribute to the national target of five million tourist arrivals, Zambia Monitor reports.

item.title: A former ambassador to Switzerland is charged with treason: police say Martha Mwitumwa, 59, plotted with persons unknown between November 2025 and 23 October 2026
item.description: The Zambia Police Service said on Monday 9 November that it had arrested and charged Martha Lungu Mwitumwa, who represented Zambia in Geneva from 2019, with treason under Section 43(1) of the Penal Code. She is in custody awaiting a court appearance. The charge is an allegation; she has not entered a plea and no response from her or a lawyer has been reported. She becomes the latest person charged with treason since the August election, after the 18 accused in the Mundubile case.

item.title: Guilty, but not going to prison: Chishimba Kambwili is convicted of unlawful assembly over a 2023 gathering at his gate and given a one-year suspended sentence
item.description: Lusaka resident magistrate Kawama Mwamfuli found on Monday 9 November that a crowd of 15 to 20 youths who sang at the former minister's Woodlands home on 26 January 2023 had turned a lawful gathering into an unlawful one, and that his role in facilitating it made him liable even though he had told them to stop. The sentence is suspended; The Zambian Observer reported that the magistrate cited his health. No appeal has been reported.

item.title: 'There are no perfect democracies': the EU and Zambia hold the dialogue Lusaka asked for in September, and Haimbe asks to comment on the observers' report before it is published
item.description: At the second EU–Zambia Extraordinary Partnership Dialogue in Lusaka on Monday 9 November, the EU's Africa director, Francesca Di Mauro, said electoral grievances should be settled through fair and impartial courts and offered support for a national process of dialogue and reconciliation. The Foreign Minister, Mulambo Haimbe, asked for the government to be allowed to comment on the Election Observation Mission's findings before its final report is published. Two days earlier the government spokesman had told the mission to leave criminal cases alone.

item.title: Brooms before breakfast: 150 commandos clear the stretch from the Universal Church to the flyover, and the council says more than 360 illegal stalls at Kamwala are gone
item.description: The Special Forces Day clean-up announced last week went ahead in Kamwala on Monday 9 November, led by Brigadier General Moses Shapwaya, The Zambian Observer reported. Lusaka City Council said in a statement the same day that it had demolished over 360 makeshift stalls at the Kamwala flyover after notices and reminders to their owners, and that the railway line had been secured, News Diggers reported. The Observer said traders had dismantled many of their own structures before the soldiers arrived.

item.title: From 20.8% to 100.9% of GDP: Musokotwane makes the case for paying tax at the budget symposium, the Treasury says Vision 2030 is on track, and NGOCC says women are left behind
item.description: At the 2027 National Budget Symposium at Mulungushi on Monday 9 November, the Finance Minister traced the debt that rose from 20.8% of GDP in 2011 to 100.9% by the end of 2021 and defended the removal of subsidies, while the Secretary to the Treasury, Felix Nkulukusa, said GDP per capita should rise from US$1,318 to US$2,985 even if some mining targets slip. News Diggers reported the minister comparing tax to a funeral contribution, and the NGOCC said the budget's withdrawal of VAT relief on energy-saving appliances will hit female-headed households.

item.title: A 180-megawatt plant for a province on a 1972 line: Stanbic and the DBSA are mandated to raise the money for Ngonye Falls, with construction pencilled in for 2027
item.description: Western Power Company has signed a mandate with Stanbic Bank Zambia and the Development Bank of Southern Africa to structure and arrange the debt for its run-of-river hydropower project on the Zambezi, Zambia Monitor reported on Monday 9 November. The developer calls it the last step before financial close. The outlets disagree on the project's size: the Monitor puts it at US$600 million, International Water Power at US$800 million. Western Province currently depends on a 66kV line built in 1972.

item.title: Ten transformers in a week and four cathodes off a moving truck: ZESCO puts its latest vandalism losses at K1.2 million as police investigate a copper theft on the Livingstone road
item.description: ZESCO recorded 23 cases of vandalism between 31 October and 5 November, 15% more than the week before, and said the loss of ten pole-mounted transformers, only three of them recovered, pushed its net loss up 317% to K1,246,931, Zambia Monitor reported on Monday 9 November. Separately, Southern Province police are investigating the theft of four copper cathode plates from a truck travelling between the Kafue weighbridge and Mazabuka on Friday 6 November, News Diggers reported.

item.title: Three in a row: Barbra Banda is named in the FIFPRO Women's World 11 again, the only player in the team from outside England and Spain, chosen by 6,511 fellow professionals
item.description: FIFPRO announced the 2026 team on Monday 9 November, as scheduled. The Orlando Pride forward is one of three strikers alongside Barcelona's Claudia Pina and Arsenal's Alessia Russo, and her third selection extends her record as the African woman with the most World 11 appearances. Players from 64 countries voted on performances between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026, a period in which Banda scored 17 NWSL goals and broke the Pride's single-season record.

item.title: Eighteen in camp, eight more on the night flight and the bonuses finally moving: Chipolopolo settle into Ndola four days before Burundi
item.description: Albert Kangwanda flew in from Dar es Salaam on Monday 9 November to join a Zambia camp already holding 18 locally based players and the captain, Fashion Sakala, ZamFoot reported, with eight more foreign-based players due that night and George Lwandamina expected to trim the group to 26. The same day the sports ministry's permanent secretary, Kangwa Chileshe, told ZNBC that the government had begun paying the outstanding winning bonuses owed to Chipolopolo and the Copper Queens.

item.title: 'Excellent diplomatic relations': Botswana's foreign minister distances his government from Ian Khama's attack on Hichilema, as Khama says he will not apologise
item.description: Dr Phenyo Butale, Botswana's Minister of International Relations, has said that the former president's description of Hakainde Hichilema as 'Africa's newest dictator' is not his government's position, and has defended Gaborone's attendance at the September inauguration, The Zambian Observer reported on Sunday 8 November. Mr Khama told the Botswana Gazette last week that he stands by his allegations. Neither report records a formal exchange between the two governments.

item.title: Andeleki warns that Zambia is no banana republic, a governance group calls the 25 November march 'shooting in the air', and a UPND official says the term-limit debate should go on
item.description: Dr Clement Andeleki said at a ministerial handover that the government would not tolerate anyone trying to throw Zambia into disarray and warned church leaders and politicians to stay within their mandate, News Diggers reported on Sunday 8 November. The paper set the remarks beside civil society's notice to the police of a march in defence of the two-term limit. Opinion on the march, and on the debate itself, is divided, including inside the ruling party.

item.title: K38.24 billion and still short of a fifth: a teachers' union says education's 13.4% of the 2027 budget is not enough, as News Diggers asks whether pupils are learning
item.description: The National Union of Public and Private Educators of Zambia welcomed the rise in the education allocation from K33.04 billion to K38.24 billion but said its 13.4% share of the K284.8 billion budget falls below the 20% international benchmark, News Diggers reported on Sunday 8 November. On the published figures, debt service will take K67.6 billion. School feeding is to rise from K523 million to K1 billion.

item.title: Three hundred jobs out of 688, and October's pay late: Daily Revelation reports a survival plan at Zambia Railways, and Kalaba asks what it says about the growth agenda
item.description: The state-owned railway's board and management have not answered reports that they proposed laying off 300 of 688 workers, Daily Revelation reports, and a staff memo dated 26 October said October salaries were delayed because operational problems had hit cash flow. Board chairperson Emmanuel Hachipuka has said jobs will have to go for the company to survive. The job-loss figure rests on one newspaper and has not been confirmed by the company.

item.title: Up six places to 15th: the 2026 Ibrahim Index puts Zambia among Africa's ten most improved on governance, on data that stop before the August election
item.description: Zambia scored 58.4 out of 100 in the Mo Ibrahim Foundation's 2026 index, a gain of 5.1 points over 2016–2025 that lifted it from 21st to 15th of 54 countries, Zambia Monitor and the Daily Nation reported last week. Citizen participation rose more than anywhere else in Africa. Satisfaction with infrastructure fell by 30.4 points. The period measured ends in 2025, before the disputed aftermath of this year's vote.

item.title: 150 Special Forces personnel and a clean-up in Kamwala: the unit marks its anniversary with the mayor's campaign on Monday, and two opposition leaders say it is the council's job
item.description: The Zambia Special Forces are to provide 150 personnel on Monday 9 November to clean the stretch between the Universal Church and the FINDECO flyover, The Zambian Observer reports, as part of the unit's annual day. Mayor Chitambala Mwewa welcomed the help. Socialist Party president Fred M'membe and Democratic Union president Ackim Njobvu have objected to elite soldiers doing municipal work. The deployment is reported by one outlet.

item.title: 'I will invite all mining firms': Hichilema hosts the under-15 champions at State House and promises to help FAZ clear a legacy debt whose size is reported two ways
item.description: The President told the squad that won Tier B of the FIFA U-15 World Cup in Baku that he would convene the mining houses to raise money for the Football Association of Zambia and help dismantle its old debt, on condition that it stops living beyond its means, ZamFoot reported on Sunday 8 November. FAZ president Keith Mweemba put the debt at not less than K40 million; the same report elsewhere says more than K140 million.

item.title: Kambole in the 93rd minute: Nkana beat NAPSA Stars 1–0 in Lusaka to go top of Stream A with 16 points from seven, and ZESCO Ndola Girls win 3–0
item.description: Lazarous Kambole scored in the third minute of stoppage time at the REIZ Arena on Sunday 8 November after NAPSA goalkeeper Charles Lawu had kept Nkana out for an hour and a half, ZamFoot reported. The win puts the Kitwe side top of their stream, with no further Stream A fixtures listed until 18 November. In the women's league, ZESCO Ndola Girls beat Konkola Blades Queens 3–0 and moved to 16 points.

item.title: Twenty-two for Ouagadougou: Mbewe names his under-23 squad for Burkina Faso on Wednesday, with Mandanji, Kalusa and Gift Siame in and Sabobo Banda out injured
item.description: Zambia's under-23s play Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou on Wednesday 11 November and at the National Heroes Stadium on Sunday 15 November in a two-legged qualifier for the 2027 Africa U23 Cup of Nations in Egypt, a tournament that doubles as a route to the 2028 Olympics. Coach Chisi Mbewe's squad has five players based in Egypt, Spain and the UAE. Midfielder Joseph Sabobo Banda was ruled out after an injury at his Armenian club.

item.title: Mobile money firms want talks, an economist names the winners and losers, and a former MP does the copper arithmetic: the 2027 budget meets its first day of scrutiny
item.description: A day after Situmbeko Musokotwane presented a K284.8 billion budget, the Mobile Money Association of Zambia said the higher transaction levies were decided without proper consultation and could undo gains in financial inclusion. Economist Lubinda Haabazoka said Social Cash Transfer households and farmers gain while consumers and mobile money users pay, and former Kamfinsa MP Christopher Kang'ombe calculated that copper output growing at its current pace reaches 1.3 million tonnes by 2031, not the three million the government is targeting.

item.title: 'Vision is freedom': Hichilema launches HH Vision 100,000, a programme to give free spectacles to learners, soldiers and the elderly, saying six million Zambians need them
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema told the Zambia Ophthalmological Society's annual conference, in a virtual address, that 100,000 pairs of spectacles have been procured for Zambians who cannot afford them. He said one in five schoolchildren struggles to see the blackboard and nearly one in three adults has poor vision, and framed the scheme as social justice rather than charity. It was piloted at three Lusaka secondary schools and at Mikango Barracks.

item.title: 'Why was the group supporting removal allowed to march?': civil society says it will go ahead on 25 November, as a UPND member abroad tells his party to end the term-limit debate
item.description: Transparency International Zambia, the Chapter One Foundation and the LCK Foundation say the government is being inconsistent in discouraging their 25 November procession in defence of presidential term limits after a petition to abolish the limits was presented to the National Assembly on 27 October and its supporters were allowed to march. The government's spokesman has called the debate imaginary. From the United States, a UPND member's Facebook live video urging the President to end the debate has been widely shared.

item.title: 'Sacrifice is met with insinuation': Saviour Chishimba answers Charles Milupi's jibe at alliance partners who leave, as the Socialist Party explains why it is skipping by-elections
item.description: Charles Milupi, who chairs the UPND Alliance Council of Presidents, said that anyone leaving the alliance now that the President has finished his appointments would show they joined only for a position; only two alliance leaders, Milupi and Felix Mutati, are in Cabinet. UPP president Saviour Chishimba replied that he was one of six people at the alliance's founding meeting in 2017 and that Milupi has been persistently inaccessible. Separately, the Socialist Party says it is skipping by-elections to rebuild after a poor August.

item.title: Nearly three in four farmers have their inputs, and some are selling them: the ministry warns against resale and shared codes as the budget plans a move from FISP to farm loans
item.description: As of Friday 6 November, 742,447 farmers, or 72.47% of the 1,024,434 targeted, had redeemed their inputs under the 2026/27 Farmer Input Support Programme, the Ministry of Agriculture said on Saturday. It also said it had received reports from several districts of farmers selling redeemed inputs to agro-dealers and sharing their e-voucher codes with cooperative leaders, and warned both farmers and dealers of action. The 2027 budget gives FISP K9.1 billion within K22.7 billion for agriculture.

item.title: 'The State does not want it heard': a defence lawyer says the prosecution fears the 18 treason accused would be freed if their bail plea is argued, before Tuesday's ruling
item.description: Milner Katolo, one of the lawyers for Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others, says the State has openly admitted it does not want their constitutional bail application heard, and that the substantive hearing will start at once if the court overrules the State's objection on Tuesday 10 November. The State argued on Thursday that the application was wrongly before the court. In Solwezi, the Subordinate Court has sent the separate sedition case to Lusaka, and Zulu has asked to represent himself.

item.title: Bronze comes home: Elisha Zimba, 17, is welcomed at Kenneth Kaunda International after his judo medal in Dakar, as Grizzly Mining backs the women's sevens with US$25,000
item.description: Elisha Zimba, who won bronze in the boys' 55 kilogram judo at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on 1 November, was met at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport by officials of the National Olympic Committee, the National Sports Council, OYDC Zambia and the Judo Association. NOCZ president Alfred Foloko, in remarks read for him, congratulated Zimba and urged companies to back young athletes before, not after, they win. Grizzly Mining has given the Zambia Rugby Union US$25,000 for the women's sevens trip to Nairobi.

item.title: Kangwa back for Bujumbura but not Ndola, Daka goes the distance for Hamburg, and Nkana visit winless Napsa on Sunday: the week before the Burundi double-header
item.description: Klings Kangwa has served the four-match ban CAF imposed after his stoppage-time red card against Morocco at AFCON 2025 and is available for the return leg in Bujumbura on 17 November, though he still misses the home qualifier at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on 13 November. Patson Daka played all 90 minutes as Hamburg beat Borussia Mönchengladbach 3–1 on Friday. In the Super League, Nkana travel to Reiz Arena on Sunday to face a Napsa Stars side still without a win.

item.title: Three nights of Chinese cinema in Lusaka: The Wandering Earth opens a four-film festival that Beijing's embassy frames around 70 years of China–Africa relations
item.description: The Zambia Chinese Film Festival ran in Lusaka from 5 to 7 November with four films, opening with the science-fiction epic The Wandering Earth. China's ambassador, Han Jing, and the Minister of Culture and Arts, Chris Chibuye, spoke at the opening ceremony, according to a statement issued by the Chinese embassy through APO Group, the only account of the event found; the minister argued that cultural and creative industries can create jobs and asked for cooperation on infrastructure, skills and financing.

item.title: K284.8 billion and half a point on VAT: Musokotwane's 2027 budget taxes mining dividends at 15%, adds a 39.5% PAYE band and aims the deficit at 3% of GDP
item.description: The Minister of Finance and National Planning, Situmbeko Musokotwane, presented a K284.8 billion budget for 2027 to the National Assembly on Friday 6 November, the largest in Zambia's history and 28.4% of GDP. Domestic revenue is to cover K233.7 billion of it, borrowing K41.9 billion and grants K9.2 billion. VAT rises from 16% to 16.5%, a 15% withholding tax lands on mining company dividends, a new 39.5% PAYE band applies to monthly pay above K37,000, and debt service alone takes K67.6 billion.

item.title: €60 million for Kapiri Mposhi–Ndola and the 1984 Railways Act to go: the budget opens the line to private trains, as Wonderful Group talks of US$1.2 billion for the southern line
item.description: The 2027 budget speech carried the first firm money for Zambia Railways in some time: an initial €60 million to rehabilitate the Kapiri Mposhi–Ndola section, reported by Zambia Monitor, with Zambia Railways to become an infrastructure manager and freight and passenger services opened to private operators. A day earlier, the Zambia Daily Mail reported that the Wonderful Group of Companies intends to put more than US$1.2 billion into rehabilitating the Livingstone–Chililabombwe line to move its cargo off the roads.

item.title: Two contracts signed, 386 kilometres of line, power by 2029: Kapala tells Parliament the Tanzania interconnector is under way, and promises no load shedding, El Niño or not
item.description: The Minister of Electricity, Peter Kapala, told the National Assembly on Thursday 5 November that Zambia's 613-kilometre share of the Zambia–Tanzania–Kenya interconnector will be commissioned in the second quarter of 2029 and will let Zambia trade up to 500 megawatts. Ecofin Agency reported that the first two of five packages, the Pensulo–Mpika and Mpika–Kasama lines, were awarded to China's Sinotec consortium on 19 October. News Diggers reported his assurance that there will be no load shedding whatever the coming rains bring.

item.title: A million hectares and more than US$100 million: the government asks the World Bank to hurry the Lobito Corridor forest project, with first activities pencilled in for January
item.description: The Minister of Green Economy and Environment, Gilbert Siame, urged a World Bank delegation in Lusaka on Thursday 5 November to speed up the design of the Lobito Corridor Integrated Forest Economy (LIFE) Project so that an agreement can be signed, Zambia Monitor reported. News Diggers reported a day earlier that the ministry's Permanent Secretary, Douty Chibamba, put the cost of the one-million-hectare plantation scheme at more than US$100 million and said preliminary work should start in January 2027.

item.title: 'You are wasting your time': Kalaba takes the EU observers' report and tells them to find a way to enforce it, as the church monitors say their own findings match the mission's
item.description: The EU Election Observation Mission has begun handing its final report to the parties. Citizens First president Harry Kalaba received it in Lusaka and, Zambia Monitor reported on Friday 6 November, agreed with its findings on ZNBC airtime, the campaign timetable and police conduct. The Zambian Observer, citing Zambian Watch, reported that he also told the observers they were wasting their time without an enforcement mechanism. The Christian Churches Monitoring Group told News Diggers its conclusions were similar to the EU's.

item.title: Three wards voted and the UPND took all three, eight contests never happened, and the President held his first rally since August: what Thursday's by-elections produced
item.description: Of the 14 by-elections the Electoral Commission scheduled for Thursday 5 November, eight could not be held after candidates withdrew, News Diggers reported; in three of the wards that did vote, Lwingishi in Mansa, Lubaleshi in Kanchibiya and Mbeta in Sioma, The Zambian Observer reported UPND wins by margins of 700, 1,960 and 163 votes. In Mandevu, where the parliamentary contest collapsed, President Hichilema held his first public rally since the general election and introduced the MP declared without a poll, the Zambia Daily Mail reported.

item.title: Two more dates: Archbishop Banda's Hilux case goes to 25 November while the DPP answers a defence application, and the treason bail panel is reported to rule on 10 November
item.description: The Archdiocese of Lusaka said on Friday that the case against Archbishop Alick Banda, charged with possessing a Toyota Hilux suspected of being unlawfully obtained, has been adjourned to Wednesday 25 November, with the Director of Public Prosecutions to respond to a defence application and the defence to reply by 18 November, ACI Africa and The Zambian Observer reported. The Observer also reported that the High Court panel hearing the bail petition of Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others will rule on the State's objection on 10 November.

item.title: 'I have done nothing wrong apart from speaking for doctors': the RDAZ president is retired in the national interest, and two opposition leaders ask the Ministry of Health why
item.description: Dr Paul Chibwe, president of the Resident Doctors Association of Zambia and an orthopaedic and trauma surgeon at Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital, told News Diggers he was handed a letter retiring him early in the national interest without an explanation. The Socialist Party's Fred M'membe asked the Ministry of Health to reverse the decision, and the OPP's Brian Mushimba said the circumstances should be established. No reason from the ministry had been published on the pages read for this edition.

item.title: Blades back on top of Stream A a day after Nkana got there, Green Eagles two clear in Stream B with one goal conceded in six, and a goalless Lusaka derby at Sunset
item.description: Konkola Blades beat Trident 2–1 at Konkola Stadium on Thursday 5 November to retake first place in Stream A of the MTN Super League transitional season with 15 points from six, two ahead of Nkana. In Stream B, Derrick Bulaya scored twice as Green Eagles won 2–0 at Chirundu United to lead by two points, while Green Buffaloes and Zesco United drew 0–0 at Sunset Stadium. Power Dynamos beat NAPSA Stars 1–0 and Nchanga Rangers beat Makeni All Stars 3–1.

item.title: A Nice midfielder, a Sheffield Wednesday forward and a point from two games: Burundi name 25 for the double-header against Zambia on 13 and 17 November
item.description: Burundi have named a 25-man squad for their two AFCON 2027 Group I qualifiers against Zambia, ZamFoot reported, led by OGC Nice midfielder Youssouf Ndayishimiye and including Sheffield Wednesday's Jordi Liongala and NAC Breda's Karim Mperanyi. Burundi are bottom of the group with one point after losing 1–0 to Togo and drawing 2–2 with Algeria in September; Zambia are second on three points, a point behind Algeria, and host the first leg at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola on Friday 13 November.

item.title: 'An imaginary issue': the government asks civil society to rethink its 25 November term-limits march, as the Evangelical Fellowship demands that the debate end now
item.description: Twelve civil society organisations have notified the police of a procession on Wednesday 25 November in defence of the two-term presidential limit, and the Evangelical Fellowship of Zambia has called for all talk of removing the limit to cease immediately. The Chief Government Spokesperson, Elvis Nkandu, replied on Thursday that every Zambian may hold an opinion but that an opinion is not a government decision, and asked the organisers why they would march against something that is not happening.

item.title: Back to Lusaka: Judge Musona moves the Mundubile–Zulu sedition case out of Solwezi, while the treason bail hearing for 18 accused is put back to Friday 6 November
item.description: Of the two decisions expected on Thursday 5 November in the cases of Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, one arrived and one did not. The Zambian Observer reports that High Court Judge Edward Musona, sitting in Solwezi, ordered the sedition case transferred to a subordinate court in Lusaka, where the two men live and were arrested. In Lusaka, the three-judge panel hearing their constitutional bail petition allowed the State to raise a fresh jurisdictional objection and adjourned to 09:00 on Friday.

item.title: Mandevu has an MP without a ballot: Adrian Banda is declared elected, a minister denies pushing out the Tonse candidate, and the ECZ says it counts votes, not makes them
item.description: The UPND's Adrian Banda was declared the winner of the Mandevu parliamentary by-election on Thursday 5 November without a vote being cast, The Zambian Observer reports, a week after his three opponents withdrew. Lusaka Province Minister Obvious Mwaliteta has denied Tonse Alliance claims that he warned the FDD's Daniel Chisenga he would 'get into trouble', and ECZ commissioner McDonald Chipenzi told agents in Sioma that the Commission counts votes and does not manufacture them.
